result.close_notes:
Root cause: checkout-api ran out of database connections to checkout-db under the campaign traffic spike (3x normal submits). Pool was 20 per pod; all pods showed active=20 with threads waiting, requests queued behind the pool and timed out.
Fix: scaled checkout-api to 12 replicas as immediate mitigation, then raised the checkout-api Hikari pool from 20 to 40 (CHG0029514) and added an HPA on checkout-api. Latency normal from 21:35 UTC.
Follow-ups: KB0009871 (checkout latency triage) written; turn on Hikari DEBUG logging so pool stats are visible next time (done for checkout-api and payments-gateway).
result.description: Customers report checkout spinning and failing at payment during the spring campaign launch. Datadog shows checkout-api p90 over 6s and 5xx around 8%. Browse is fine.
result.short_description: Checkout slow and timing out during spring campaign

result.close_notes: The origin certificate expired at 09:04 ET. The renewal job still pointed at a retired origin hostname, so it never fired. Certificate reissued and deployed to the origin at 09:31 ET, and the 502s cleared within two minutes. Added an expiry monitor on all CDN origin certificates alerting at 30 and 7 days, and corrected the hostname list in the renewal job.
result.description: Synthetic checks against the storefront have returned HTTP 502 from the edge in every region since about 09:05 ET. The CDN origin certificate appears to have expired.
result.short_description: Storefront 502s for about 25 min after CDN origin TLS certificate expired

result.close_notes: The relay host root volume reached 100 percent at 12:58 ET, so the queue stopped spooling and then drained slowly once space was freed. Old bounce logs and the spool archive were removed, the volume was extended by 40 GB, and the queue was empty by 15:38 ET. Follow-up: move the relay spool onto its own volume and add a disk alert at 80 percent.
result.description: Customer service reports order confirmation emails arriving up to two hours after purchase. The SMTP relay queue is backing up and nothing is failing outright.
result.short_description: Order confirmation emails delayed up to 2 hours, SMTP relay queue backlog

result.close_notes: The indexer memory limit was 1.5 GiB, and the catalog snapshot it loads had grown past that after the spring range expansion. The limit was raised to 3 GiB with a 2 GiB request, and the job was re-run by hand so the index is current. Follow-up: add a memory alert on the job and review snapshot size each quarter.
result.description: The product search indexer cron job on k8s-prod-east has been OOMKilled on every run since 02:00 ET. Storefront search is returning catalog data from about a day ago.
result.short_description: Search indexer cron OOMKilled, product search results a day old

result.close_notes: Image garbage collection only started at 90 percent root disk usage, so unused storefront image layers built up until kubelet eviction started first. Image GC thresholds were lowered to start at 70 percent and stop at 60 percent, and the evicted pods rescheduled cleanly. Follow-up: move image storage to the larger data disk when the nodes are rebuilt.
result.description: Two k8s-prod-east nodes reported DiskPressure at about 22:05 ET and storefront pods were evicted from both. Remaining replicas are serving traffic but the deployment is below its desired count.
result.short_description: Node disk pressure evicted storefront pods on two k8s-prod-east nodes

result.close_notes:
PayCore had a full outage from 16:02 to 16:44 UTC (their incident, confirmed on their status page). payments-gateway failed fast as designed: every authorize call hit the 3000ms PSP timeout and returned a decline to checkout, so customers saw "card declined" and could retry later. No knock-on to pay-db-01 or the gateway pools; connections stayed at baseline throughout.
No action on our side beyond customer comms. Recovered when PayCore recovered.
Follow-up: PAY-2231 (PSP client resilience) to look at retrying transient PSP failures so short PayCore blips don't decline good cards.
result.description: Payment authorizations failing for all card payments. payments-gateway logs show PSP timeouts on every call to api.paycore.example. PayCore status page shows major outage.
result.short_description: Card payments failing - PayCore outage

result.close_notes: The provider's monthly request quota on our plan ran out at about 14:50 ET after a campaign pushed checkout traffic past the plan allowance. Checkout fell back to local validation rules as designed, so no orders were blocked. The plan quota was raised with the provider and the client now backs off on 429 responses before it falls back. Follow-up: alert on quota usage at 80 percent of the monthly allowance.
result.description: Checkout address validation calls to the external provider have returned HTTP 429 since 14:50 ET, and the Checkout API has switched to local rules. Orders are completing, but address suggestions and standardization are not being applied.
result.short_description: Address validation fell back to local rules after provider HTTP 429

result.close_notes: Old finance export files from the previous year, about 180 GB in total, filled C: and the report writes its staging file there. The files were moved to the archive share and the report was re-run by hand, finishing at 07:15 ET. Follow-up: a scheduled cleanup job will remove exports older than 30 days from C: and is in review.
result.description: The nightly finance report on win-rpt-06 failed at 02:10 ET with a disk write error. The C: drive has no free space left.
result.short_description: Nightly finance report failed on win-rpt-06, C: drive full

result.close_notes: The acquirer's settlement file for the previous business day arrived with 14 columns where the agreed layout has 15, and the parser stopped on the first malformed row and held the whole run. The acquirer re-sent the file, and the reconciliation completed at 14:10 ET and matched all records. The parser now rejects any file with the wrong column count or header at intake and raises an alert to the payments on-call channel.
result.description: The refund settlement reconciliation has not started because the parser rejected the acquirer's settlement file for the previous business day. The run is expected to finish late this afternoon.
result.short_description: Refund settlement reconciliation 3 hours late, acquirer file malformed

result.close_notes:
Benign. Fragmentation ratio swings between 1.3 and 1.6 on a ~2 hour cycle with the session expiry pattern; activedefrag handles it. No evictions, no latency impact on login or checkout. Sessions moved to the redis cluster last year so this instance only holds legacy keys.
Follow-up: raise the monitor threshold or retire the monitor (not done yet).
result.description: Datadog monitor 'redis-sessions memory fragmentation high' alerting, ratio 1.6. Paged Platform.
result.short_description: redis-sessions memory fragmentation high

result.close_notes: Image resizer pods were limited to 500m CPU, which was too low for the resize volume after the new hero image sizes went live, so CPU throttling capped them under load. The CPU limit was raised to 2 CPU with the request unchanged, and p90 product page time returned to under 1 s by 18:55 ET. Follow-up: add a CPU throttling panel for the resizer and revisit the limit after the next catalog image change.
result.description: Product page p90 response time on the storefront has risen to about 3 s since 16:20 ET. The image resizer pods show sustained CPU throttling and product images are slow to load.
result.short_description: Product pages slow (p90 3 s), image resizer pods CPU throttled
